_comment: T004 mitigation: least-privilege execution role example for AgentCore Runtime. Replace <REGION>, <ACCOUNT_ID>, <RUNTIME_ID>, and the model ARN with your values. Any code running in the AgentCore microVM can read these credentials via the instance metadata endpoint (MMDS), so scope this role to only what the agent needs (per https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-security-best-practices.html). Do NOT ship the broad CLI-generated dev policy to production.

Statement._comment: CreateInference authorizes the inference; CallWithBearerToken is also required when authenticating with a Bedrock API key / bearer token (as the OpenAI SDK does via aws-bedrock-token-generator). Without CallWithBearerToken the OpenAI-SDK call fails 403 'not authorized to perform: bedrock-mantle:CallWithBearerToken'. Note: mantle takes the bare model id (openai.gpt-5.6-terra); the us. inference-profile id is a bedrock-runtime concept and returns 404 on mantle. The profile ARN is retained here only for a bedrock-runtime fallback.

Grants the two Web Search actions the example uses. Resource is '*' because bedrock-websearch actions (InvokeSearch/InvokeFetch) do not support resource-level scoping — there is no per-search resource ARN to name, so '*' is the only valid form (see the Service Authorization Reference for Amazon Bedrock Web Search). The privilege is instead constrained three ways: (1) only these two actions are granted, not the broader bedrock-websearch:*; (2) bedrock-websearch:ExternalWebAccess is intentionally omitted, so with external_web_access=false retrieval stays inside the AWS boundary (Search from the Bedrock web index, Fetch from the Bedrock cache); and (3) the aws:RequestedRegion condition below pins usage to the Web Search-supported Region this agent runs in.
